paragraphs: Accendra Health, Inc. (f/k/a Owens & Minor, Inc.) and subsidiaries (Accendra Health, we, us, our or the Company) is a leading nationwide provider of products, technology, and services that supports health beyond the hospital for millions of people each year. We connect patients, providers, and insurers, delivering innovative solutions that help promote better health outcomes and improve quality of life for people living with chronic, complex, and acute health conditions. Together, our trusted brands, Apria and Byram Healthcare, bring nearly 90 years of combined experience in promoting health beyond the hospital in communities across the country. We are headquartered in Richmond, Virginia. The description of our business should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and supplementary data included in this Form 10-K.

On October 7, 2025, we entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement, (the Purchase Agreement) by and among the Company, Dominion Healthcare Acquisition Corporation, a Delaware corporation (the Purchaser), and Dominion Healthcare Holdings, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (Purchaser Parent) to sell the Products & Healthcare Services (P&HS) business, for an aggregate of $375 million in cash, subject to certain adjustments for cash, indebtedness, net working capital and transaction expenses. On December 31, 2025, we completed the sale of the P&HS business pursuant to the Purchase Agreement. We have retained a 5% equity interest in the P&HS business.

We provide delivery of products, including disposable medical supplies sold directly to patients and home health agencies and are a leading provider of integrated home healthcare equipment and related services in the U.S. We offer a comprehensive range of products and services for in-home care and delivery across diabetes treatment, home respiratory therapy (including home oxygen and non-invasive ventilation services), and obstructive sleep apnea treatment (including continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and bi-level positive airway pressure devices, and patient support services). Additionally, we supply a wide range of other home medical equipment, patient care product lines including ostomy, wound care (including negative pressure wound therapy), urology, incontinence and other products and services to help improve the quality of life for patients with home care needs. Revenues are generated through fee-for-service and capitation arrangements with large government and commercial payors (Payors) for equipment, supplies, services and other items rented and sold to patients. We provide patients with a variety of clinical and administrative support services and related products and supplies, most of which are prescribed by a physician as part of a care plan. We are one of the industry's highest-quality providers of home healthcare equipment, medical supplies and related services, while maintaining a commitment to being a low-cost operator. We aim to provide a compelling value proposition to patients, providers and Payors by allowing patients to receive necessary care and services in the comfort of their own home, while, at the same time, reducing the costs of treatment. We use technology in areas such as web portals/electronic ordering, electronic claims submission and electronic funds transfer with managed care organizations to more efficiently process business transactions. This use of technology can improve the initial patient admission process, expedite claims processing and reduce the administrative costs associated with this activity for both us and our providers and Payors.

We provide equipment and disposable medical supplies rented and sold directly to patients and home health agencies, for which payments are received from managed care plans, the U.S. federal government under the Medicare program, state governments under their respective Medicaid or similar programs, private insurers, home health agencies, and directly from patients. Medicare contracts may be subject to a Competitive Bidding Process (CBP) for durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies (DMEPOS), as further described in the Regulation section.

Accendra Health has internal expertise to manage the unique reimbursement requirements of certain Payors and continue to negotiate simplifications in the claims submission process in an effort to reduce subsequent denials and shorten related collection periods. Our general practice is to collect co-payments from the patient or applicable secondary Payor.

We actively manage our accounts receivable to minimize credit risk, days sales outstanding (DSO) and accounts receivable carrying costs. We have ongoing initiatives to improve our collections. Our ability to accurately invoice and ship product to customers enhances our collection results and affects our DSO performance. As we diversify our customer portfolio, the change in business mix also affects our DSO.

The industry in which we operate is highly competitive. We compete with many healthcare companies across a variety of channels to provide medical supplies and related services for in-home care. We compete against national providers and numerous regional and local providers that deliver products and services to patients' homes, including AdaptHealth Corp., Lincare, Inogen, Viemed Healthcare, Inc., Quipt Home Medical, Cardinal Health and Rotech. In addition, pharmacy benefit managers, such as CVS Health Corporation, compete with us in the home healthcare market.
We have trademarks in the U.S. that are used to designate or identify our Company. We operate under registered trademarks Accendra Health, Apria, Byram Healthcare and Lofta.

Our business is subject to federal and state laws and regulations over our operations, including the reimbursement of our products and services under various government programs that are designed to prevent fraud and abuse. We are subject to state laws governing pharmacies, nursing services, medical equipment suppliers and certain types of home health activities. Our teammates are subject to state laws and regulations governing certain professional licensure, including for respiratory therapy, pharmacy and nursing. Compliance with laws and regulations is costly and materially affects our business. We believe we are in material compliance with all statutes and regulations applicable to our operations. Notwithstanding this, violations of these laws and regulations may still occur, which could subject us to civil and criminal enforcement actions; licensure revocation, suspension, or non-renewal; severe fines and penalties; the repayment of amounts previously paid to us; and even the termination of our ability to provide services under certain government programs.

Healthcare is an industry of rapid regulatory change. Changes in the laws and regulations and new interpretations of or guidelines relating to existing laws and regulations may affect permissible activities and compliance requirements, licenses and approvals required to be held, the relative costs associated with doing business, and reimbursement amounts paid by federal, state and other third-party Payors. We cannot predict the future of federal, state and local regulation or legislation, or possible changes in national healthcare policies. Future legislative and regulatory changes could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

Numerous federal and state laws and regulations, including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), as amended by the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (HITECH), govern the collection, dissemination, security, use and confidentiality of Protected Health Information (PHI). HIPAA includes a number of requirements pertaining to the privacy and security of certain PHI, as well as the standard formatting of certain electronic health transactions. As part of the provision of, and billing for, healthcare equipment and

services, we are required to collect and maintain PHI and as such, are subject to HIPAA as a covered entity. HIPAA also applies to business associates of covered entities, which are individuals and entities that provide services for or on behalf of those covered entities. Failure of our business associates to comply with HIPAA requirements can adversely impact our business. Numerous other federal and state laws that protect the confidentiality, privacy, availability, integrity and security of PHI and healthcare related data also apply to us. In many cases, these laws are more restrictive than, and not preempted by, the HIPAA and HITECH rules and requirements, and may be subject to varying interpretation by courts and government agencies, creating complex compliance issues for us and potentially exposing us to additional expenses, adverse publicity and liability.

Further, federal and state consumer laws are being applied increasingly by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state enforcement authorities, to regulate the collection, use and disclosure of personal information or PHI, and to ensure that businesses and organizations maintaining personal information about individuals implement appropriate data safeguards. For instance, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) became effective on January 1, 2020. The CCPA gives California residents expanded rights to direct the use of their personal information. The CCPA provides for civil penalties for violations, as well as a private right of action for data breaches that may result in data breach litigation. Although there are limited exemptions for PHI and HIPAA regulated entities, and the CCPA's implementation standards and enforcement practices are continuing to develop and remain uncertain for the foreseeable future, the CCPA may increase our compliance costs and potential liability. In November 2020, Californians approved the California Privacy Rights Act (the CPRA), which modified and expanded the CCPA and established a new California Privacy Protection Agency. The CPRA established January 1, 2023 as the new compliance date for most of the other substantive provisions of the CPRA. Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, and Virginia have enacted similar laws to provide for the protection of consumer privacy, and numerous other states have similar laws under consideration. Additionally, in 2023, Washington state passed the My Health My Data Act ("MHMDA") — a comprehensive data privacy law that imposes significant obligations on entities doing business or targeting consumers in Washington and creates a private right of action that may invite an influx of litigation. Some of the MHMDA's provisions went into effect in July 2023 and in March 2024. The Florida Legislature passed an update to the Florida Electronic Health Records Exchange Act, effective since 2023, that prohibits health care providers that use certified health record technologies from storing electronic health records outside the United States, its territories, or Canada. The ban also applies to patient information stored through a third-party or subcontracted computing facility or cloud computing service.

Additionally, the FTC and many state attorneys general are interpreting existing federal and state consumer protection laws to impose evolving standards for the online collection, use, dissemination and security of PHI and other personal information. Courts may also adopt the standards for fair information practices promulgated by the FTC, which concern consumer notice, choice, security, and access. Consumer protection laws require us to publish statements that describe how we handle personal information and choices individuals may have about the way we handle their personal information. If we publish information that is considered untrue, it may be subject to government claims of unfair or deceptive trade practices, which could lead to significant liabilities and consequences. Furthermore, according to the FTC, violating consumers' privacy rights or failing to take appropriate steps to keep consumers' personal information secure may constitute unfair acts or practices in or affecting commerce in violation of Section 5 of the FTC Act.

paragraphs: On February 28, 2025, we announced that we were actively engaged in discussions regarding the potential sale of our Products & Healthcare Services business. On October 7, 2025, we entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement (the Purchase Agreement) by and among the Company, Dominion Healthcare Acquisition Corporation, a Delaware

corporation (the Purchaser), and Dominion Healthcare Holdings, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (Purchaser Parent) to sell the P&HS business, for an aggregate of $375 million in cash, subject to certain adjustments for cash, indebtedness, net working capital and transaction expenses. On December 31, 2025, we completed the sale of the P&HS business pursuant to the Purchase Agreement. We retained a 5% equity interest in the P&HS business.

In accordance with GAAP, the financial position and results of operations of the P&HS business are presented as discontinued operations and, as such, have been excluded from continuing operations for all periods presented. With the exception of Note 3, the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements reflect the continuing operations of Accendra Health, Inc. unless otherwise noted. See Note 3 in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information regarding discontinued operations.

Accendra Health, Inc. (f/k/a Owens & Minor, Inc.) and subsidiaries (Accendra Health, we, us, our or the Company) is a leading nationwide provider of products, technology, and services that supports health beyond the hospital for millions of people each year. As discussed later within Note 1 to Consolidated Financial Statements, our business activities comprise a single operating and reporting segment.

Net (loss) per share from continuing operations was $(1.34) for the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to net (loss) per share from continuing operations of $(4.57) for the year ended December 31, 2024. Our financial results for the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to the prior year were favorably impacted by the following: (1) no goodwill impairment charges for the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to charges incurred for the year ended December 31, 2024 of $307 million, or a $3.97 negative impact per share (see Notes 1 and 5 in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements); (2) revenue growth of $82 million; (3) a reduction in exit and realignment charges of $28 million; (4) the remeasurement of an uncertain tax position for the year ended December 31, 2024, including interest which resulted in a $19 million, or a $0.24 negative income tax charge per share (see Note 12 in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements); that did not reoccur and (5) a $15 million reduction in selling, general and administrative expense. These impacts were partially offset by (1) an $80 million transaction breakage fee incurred in connection with the termination of the Rotech acquisition; (2) an increase in cost of net revenue of $73 million; (3) an increase in intangible amortization of $33 million; and (4) $18 million in transaction fees during the year ended December 31, 2025.

Net (loss) per share from continuing operations was $(4.57) for the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to net income per share from continuing operations of $0.12 for the year ended December 31, 2023. Our financial results for the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the prior year were unfavorably impacted by the following: (1) a goodwill impairment charge incurred for the year ended December 31, 2024 of $307 million, or a $3.97 negative impact per share; (2) an $81 million increase in selling, general, and administrative expenses including legal settlements of $17 million related primarily to compensation and wage and hour disputes; (3) a $64 million increase in cost of net revenue; and (4) a $39 million increase in exit and realignment costs. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by (1) a $128 million increase in net revenue; (2) a decrease in intangible amortization of $18 million; and (3) a $9.2 million decrease in interest expense, net.
Refer to "Results of Operations" for further detail of quantitative and qualitative drivers of our results.

As previously disclosed, on July 22, 2024, we entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the Merger Agreement) pursuant to which we agreed to acquire Rotech Healthcare Holdings Inc. (Rotech) subject to the terms and conditions within the Merger Agreement. On June 3, 2025, the Company, Rotech and Merger Sub mutually agreed to terminate the Merger Agreement and entered into a mutual termination agreement (the Termination Agreement). In accordance with the terms of the Termination Agreement, on June 5, 2025, we made a cash payment to Rotech of $80 million.

A commercial Payor, with which we have multiple separately managed contracts, has terminated, or is in the process of terminating, certain of our contracts with them. This termination resulted in minimal impacts to our operating income for the year ended December 31, 2025, as the transitions of agreements and services started late in the fourth quarter of 2025. While such transitions of agreements and services are expected to continue throughout the first half of 2026, the specific timing of when these contracts will wind down is highly dependent on the Payor's successor provider's ability to successfully transition customers among other factors. The terminated contracts reflected $322 million or 12% of our net revenue, including $231 million of capitation revenue, which represents nearly all of our capitation revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2025.

paragraphs: Accendra Health, Inc. (f/k/a Owens & Minor, Inc.) 及其子公司 (Accendra Health, 我們, 我們, 我們或本公司) 是一家領先的全國性供應產品、技術及服務的公司，每年為數百萬人提供超出醫院範疇的健康支持。我們連結病患、醫療提供者與保險機構，提供創新解決方案，協助促進更好的健康結果，並改善患有慢性、複雜及急性健康問題的民眾的生活品質。我們受信賴的品牌 Apria 及 Byram Healthcare，共同擁有近 90 年的經驗，推動社區內的健康照護。本公司總部設於維吉尼亞州里奇蒙。本公司業務說明應與本 Form 10-K 所包含的合併財務報表及補充資料一併閱讀。

於 2025 年 10 月 7 日，本公司與 Dominion Healthcare Acquisition Corporation，一家德拉瓦州公司 (購買方)，以及 Dominion Healthcare Holdings, L.P.，一家德拉瓦州有限合夥企業 (購買方母公司) 籤訂股份買賣協議 (買賣協議)，出售 Products & Healthcare Services (P&HS) 事業，總計現金為 375 百萬美元，扣除現金、負債、淨營運資金及交易費用後的調整金額。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司根據買賣協議完成 P&HS 事業的出售。本公司保留 P&HS 事業 5% 的股權。

我們提供產品的配送，包括直接銷售給病患及居家照護機構的消耗性醫療用品，並為美國提供整合式居家醫療設備及相關服務的領先供應商。我們提供涵蓋居家照護及配送的全面產品與服務，包括糖尿病治療、居家呼吸治療 (包括居家氧氣及非侵入性通氣服務) 以及阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症治療 (包括持續正壓通氣 (CPAP) 及雙水平正壓通氣裝置，以及病患支持服務)。此外，我們供應廣泛的其他居家醫療設備、病患照護產品線，包括造口、傷口照護 (包括負壓傷口治療)、泌尿科、失禁及其他產品與服務，以協助改善有居家照護需求病患的生活品質。收入來自與大型政府及商業保險機構 (保險機構) 的費用服務及按人頭計費安排，提供設備、用品、服務及其他租賃與銷售給病患的項目。我們為病患提供多樣的臨牀與行政支持服務及相關產品與用品，大多數由醫師開立為照護計畫的一部分。我們是居家醫療設備、醫療用品及相關服務的行業最高品質供應商，同時致力於成為低成本運營者。我們旨在為病患、醫療提供者及保險機構提供有吸引力的價值主張，讓病患能在家中舒適的環境接受必要的照護與服務，同時降低治療成本。我們在網路入口網站/電子訂購、電子申報及電子資金轉帳等領域使用科技，以更有效率地處理業務交易。這種科技的應用可以改善病患入院流程，加快申報處理速度，並降低我們與醫療提供者及保險機構相關的行政成本。
我們提供租賃及直接銷售給病患及居家照護機構的設備與消耗性醫療用品，付款來自管理式醫療計畫、美國聯邦政府根據 Medicare 計畫、各州政府根據其 Medicaid 或類似計畫、私人保險機構、居家照護機構，以及直接來自病患。Medicare 合約可能根據耐用醫療設備、假肢、矯形器及用品 (DMEPOS) 面臨競爭性招標程序 (CBP)，如 Regulation 節進一步說明。
Accendra Health 具備內部專業知識，以管理某些保險機構的獨特賠付要求，並持續與保險機構協商簡化申報程序，以減少後續拒絕付款及縮短相關收款週期。我們的一般做法是向病患或適用的次級保險機構收取共付額。
我們積極管理應收帳款，以降低信用風險、應收帳款週轉天數 (DSO) 及應收帳款攜帶成本。我們有持續改善收款的計畫。我們準確發票及發送產品給客戶的能力，會提升我們的收款結果，並影響我們的 DSO 表現。隨著我們擴展客戶組合，業務組合的變化也會影響我們的 DSO。

我們所處的行業競爭激烈。我們與許多醫療公司透過多種渠道競爭，提供居家照護所需的醫療用品及相關服務。我們與全國性供應商及許多區域性與地方性供應商競爭，這些供應商將產品與服務提供給病患家中，包括 AdaptHealth Corp.、Lincare、Inogen、Viemed Healthcare, Inc.、Quipt Home Medical、Cardinal Health 及 Rotech。此外，藥物福利管理機構，如 CVS Health Corporation，也在居家醫療市場與我們競爭。
我們在美國擁有用以標示或識別本公司之商標。我們在註冊商標 Accendra Health、Apria、Byram Healthcare 及 Lofta 下運營。

本公司業務受聯邦及州法律與規範之制約，包括各項政府計畫對本公司產品與服務之補償，這些計畫旨在防止詐欺與濫用。本公司受州法律規範藥房、護理服務、醫療器材供應商及某些類型居家照護活動。本公司員工受州法律與規範之制約，包括某些專業執照，如呼吸治療、藥劑與護理。遵守法律與規範成本高昂，且對本公司業務產生重大影響。本公司相信本公司已符合所有適用於本公司業務之法律與規範。 notwithstanding this, 違反這些法律與規範仍可能發生，這可能使本公司面臨民事與刑事執法行動；執照吊銷、暫停或不續約；嚴重罰款與處罰；需歸還先前支付予本公司之金額；甚至終止本公司在某些政府計畫下提供服務之資格。
醫療保健產業為快速變動之規範產業。法律與規範之變更，以及對現有法律與規範之新解釋或指引，可能影響允許之活動與合規要求、必須持有之許可與核准、營運之相對成本，以及聯邦、州及其他第三方付款人支付之補償金額。本公司無法預測聯邦、州及地方之規範或立法之未來，或可能之國家醫療保健政策變更。未來之立法與規範變更可能對本公司財務狀況、營運結果與現金流產生重大不利影響。

眾多聯邦及州法律與規範，包括《健康保險可攜性與責任法案》（HIPAA），經2009年《健康資訊科技促進經濟與臨牀健康法案》（HITECH）修正後，規範保護健康資訊（PHI）之收集、散佈、安全、使用與保密。HIPAA包含若干關於特定PHI之隱私權與安全性的要求，以及特定電子健康交易之標準格式要求。作為提供及計費醫療器材與服務之一環，本公司被要求收集並保存PHI，因此本公司作為被規範實體，受HIPAA之制約。HIPAA亦適用於被規範實體之業務夥伴，即為被規範實體提供服務或代表被規範實體之個人與機構。若本公司業務夥伴未能遵守HIPAA之要求，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。眾多其他聯邦及州法律亦規範PHI與醫療相關資料之保密性、隱私權、可用性、完整性與安全性，並適用於本公司。在許多情況下，這些法律比HIPAA與HITECH之規則與要求更為嚴格，且未被HIPAA與HITECH規則與要求所預先適用，且可能因法院與政府機構之不同解釋，使本公司面臨複雜之合規問題，並可能使本公司面臨額外費用、不利公眾聲譽與責任。

進一步而言，聯邦與州消費者法律正被聯邦貿易委員會（FTC）與州執法機關日益廣泛地應用，以規範個人資訊或PHI之收集、使用與揭露，並確保維護個人資訊之機構與組織實施適當之資料安全措施。例如，加州消費者隱私權法案（CCPA）於2020年1月1日生效。CCPA賦予加州居民更廣泛的權利，以掌控其個人資訊之使用。CCPA對違反行為設有民事處罰，並賦予私人訴訟權利，可能導致資料洩漏之訴訟。儘管PHI與HIPAA規範實體有有限之豁免，且CCPA之實施標準與執法實務仍在發展中，且在可預見之未來仍不確定，CCPA可能增加本公司之合規成本與潛在責任。2020年11月，加州選民批准了《加州隱私權權利法案》（CPRA），該法案修改並擴充CCPA，並設立新的加州隱私權保護機構。CPRA將CPRA其他實質條款之新合規日期設為2023年1月1日。科羅拉多州、康涅狄格州、猶他州與維吉尼亞州已頒布類似法律，以保護消費者隱私權，且許多其他州正在考慮類似法律。此外，2023年華盛頓州通過《我的健康我的資料法案》（MHMDA）——一項全面資料隱私權法，對在華盛頓州營運或針對華盛頓州消費者之機構施加重大義務，並設立私人訴訟權利，可能引發訴訟浪潮。MHMDA部分條款於2023年7月生效，並於2024年3月生效。佛羅裏達州立法機構已更新《佛羅裏達電子健康記錄交換法案》，自2023年起生效，禁止使用認證健康記錄技術之醫療保健提供者將電子健康記錄儲存於美國、其屬地或加拿大以外之地區，該禁令也適用於透過第三方或 subcontracted 計算機設施或雲端計算服務儲存之患者資訊。

此外，聯邦與州級消費者法規正被聯邦貿易委員會（FTC）及州級執法機關 increasingly 用來規範個人資訊或 PHI 的收集、使用與揭露，並確保維護個人資訊的企業與組織實施適當的資料安全措施。例如，加州消費者隱私權法案（CCPA）於 2020 年 1 月 1 日生效。CCPA 給加州居民擴展的權利，以主導其個人資訊的使用。CCPA 對違反規定設有民事處罰，並賦予私人提告權利，可能導致資料洩漏的訴訟。儘管 PHI 及 HIPAA 規範機構有有限的豁免，且 CCPA 的執行標準與執法方式仍在持續發展且未來一段時間仍不確定，CCPA 可能增加我們的合規成本與潛在責任。2020 年 11 月，加州選民批准了加州隱私權權利法案（CPRA），該法案修改並擴展了 CCPA，並設立了新的加州隱私權保護機構。CPRA 將大多數其他實質條款的合規日期設為 2023 年 1 月 1 日。科羅拉多州、康涅狄格州、猶他州與弗吉尼亞州已通過類似法律以保護消費者隱私權，且許多其他州正在考慮類似法律。此外，2023 年，華盛頓州通過了「我的健康我的資料法案」（My Health My Data Act，MHMDA）——一項全面的資料隱私權法，對在華盛頓州營業或針對華盛頓州消費者進行業務的實體施加重大義務，並設立私人提告權利，可能引發大量訴訟。MHMDA 的部分條款於 2023 年 7 月生效，並於 2024 年 3 月生效。佛羅裏達州立法機構通過了對佛羅裏達州電子健康記錄交換法案的更新，自 2023 年起生效，禁止使用認證健康記錄技術的醫療保健提供者將電子健康記錄儲存於美國、其屬地或加拿大的境外。禁令也適用於透過第三方或分包計算設施或雲端計算服務儲存的患者資訊。

Furthermore, according to the FTC, violating consumers' privacy rights or failing to take appropriate steps to keep consumers' personal information secure may constitute unfair acts or practices in or affecting commerce in violation of Section 5 of the FTC Act.

paragraphs: 2025 年 2 月 28 日，本公司宣佈，我們正在積極進行有關出售本公司產品與醫療服務業務之潛在交易的討論。2025 年 10 月 7 日，本公司與本公司、Dominion Healthcare Acquisition Corporation，一家特拉華州公司（買方）、以及 Dominion Healthcare Holdings, L.P.，一家特拉華州有限合夥企業（買方母公司）簽訂了股份購買協議（購買協議），以出售 P&HS 業務，總計現金為 375 百萬美元，並根據現金、負債、淨營運資金及交易費用進行調整。2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司根據購買協議完成了 P&HS 業務的出售。本公司保留 P&HS 業務 5% 的股權。
公司（買受人），以及Dominion Healthcare Holdings, L.P., 一家Delaware有限責任合夥企業（買受人母公司）同意出售P&HS業務，總計現金為375 百萬美元，扣除現金、負債、淨營運資金及交易費用後的調整後金額。於2025年12月31日，我們根據買賣協議完成了P&HS業務的出售。我們保留P&HS業務5%的權益。
Accendra Health, Inc.（原名 Owens & Minor, Inc.）及其子公司（Accendra Health、本公司、我們、我們或本公司）是美國全國知名的產品、技術與服務供應商，每年支持數百萬人實現健康照護，超越醫院範疇。如後續於合併財務報表附註 1 所討論，本公司業務活動僅包含一個營運及報告分部。
Accendra Health, Inc.（原名 Owens & Minor, Inc.）及其子公司（Accendra Health、本公司、我們、我們或本公司）是美國全國知名的產品、技術與服務供應商，每年支持數百萬人實現健康照護，超越醫院範疇。如後續於合併財務報表附註 1 所討論，本公司業務活動僅包含一個營運及報告分部。

每股持續運營業務的淨虧損為 1.34 美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年每股持續運營業務的淨虧損 4.57 美元相比。我們 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年的財務結果，與前一年相比，受到以下因素正面影響：(1) 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年未發生商譽減損費用，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年發生的 307 百萬美元費用相比，每股市價負面影響為 3.97 美元（請參閱合併財務陳述附註第 1 與第 5 項）；(2) 收入成長 82 百萬美元；(3) 出口與重整費用減少 28 百萬美元；(4) 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年重新衡量不確定稅務地位，包括利息，導致每股市價負面收入稅費用為 19 百萬美元，或 0.24 美元（請參閱合併財務陳述附註第 12 項）；此影響未重複發生，(5) 売貨、一般及行政費用減少 15 百萬美元。這些影響部分被以下因素抵銷：(1) 連帶終止 Rotech 收購所產生的 80 百萬美元交易違約費用；(2) 網路收入成本增加 73 百萬美元；(3) 無形資產攤銷增加 33 百萬美元；以及 (4) 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年產生的 18 百萬美元交易費用。

每股持續運營業務的淨虧損為 4.57 美元，為 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年，與 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年每股持續運營業務的淨收入 0.12 美元相比。我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年的財務結果，與前一年相比，受到以下因素負面影響：(1) 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年發生的商譽減損費用為 307 百萬美元，每股市價負面影響為 3.97 美元；(2) 売貨、一般及行政費用增加 81 百萬美元，包括與主要涉及薪資與工時爭議的法律和解費用 17 百萬美元；(3) 網路收入成本增加 64 百萬美元；以及 (4) 出口與重整費用增加 39 百萬美元。這些負面影響部分被以下因素抵銷：(1) 網路收入增加 128 百萬美元；(2) 無形資產攤銷減少 18 百萬美元；以及 (3) 利息費用，淨減少 9.2 百萬美元。
請參閱 "營運成果" 以取得更多關於我們營運成果的量化與質化驅動因素的詳細資訊。

如先前所披露，我們於 2024 年 7 月 22 日與 Rotech Healthcare Holdings Inc. (Rotech) 籤訂合併協議 (合併協議)，並同意以符合合併協議的條件與條款取得 Rotech。於 2025 年 6 月 3 日，本公司、Rotech 與合併子公司 mutually 同意終止合併協議，並簽訂相互終止協議 (終止協議)。根據終止協議的條款，我們於 2025 年 6 月 5 日向 Rotech 支付 80 百萬美元現金。

一家商業性付費者，與我們有數個獨立管理的契約，已終止，或正在終止部分與我們的契約。此終止導致我們於2025年12月31日財年營運收入的影響極小，因協議與服務的過渡在2025年第四季末才開始。雖然這些協議與服務的過渡預期將持續至2026年上半年，但這些契約何時會結束，高度取決於付費者繼任供應商能否成功過渡客戶等其他因素。已終止的契約反映2025年12月31日財年我們的淨營收為322 百萬美元，佔12%，其中包括231 百萬美元的資本化收入，這幾乎代表我們所有的資本化收入。
本年度報告10-K中「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」部分，討論了2025年、2024年及2023年的項目以及2025年、2024年與2023年之間的年對年比較。

客戶與產品組成的可能變動，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、資本資源及流動性產生重大不利影響。

目前及未來經濟狀況的不確定性及其他一般政治環境的不利變動，可能對本公司產品及服務的需求及應收帳款的可收回性產生不利影響。

本報告包含若干聲明，屬於 1995 年私人證券 litigation 改革法案 所定義的 "forward-looking statements"（展望性聲明）。展望性聲明包含所有不單純與歷史或現狀事實相關的聲明，通常可透過使用 "may"、"could"、"aim"、"seek"、"believe"、"will"、"expect"、"project"、"estimate"、"intend"、"target"、"anticipate"、"plan"、"continue" 或類似詞彙來辨識。本年度報告中的展望性聲明係基於若干風險與不確定性，包括下列風險因素及 herein 討論的特定風險因素，以及本年度報告中與展望性聲明相關的其他部分所討論的風險因素，這些因素可能導致實際結果與展望性聲明所表達或暗示的預期與預測有重大差異。導致這種差異的風險與不確定性包括，但不僅限於：市場中競爭與價格壓力的增加；我們保留現有客戶與吸引新客戶的能力，以及我們對某些客戶、供應商、供應鏈及第三方的依賴；我們成功識別、管理或整合收購的能力；來自我們營運市場之法律、監管或許可要求的風險；以及總體經濟、監管與營運條件，包括與我們國際業務相關的條件，等等。隨時間推移，可能出現新的風險與不確定性，且難以預測。儘管我們相信展望性聲明的預期是基於對我們業務與營運的合理假設，且在我們知識範圍內，所有展望性聲明均涉及風險與不確定性，因此實際結果可能與這些聲明所預測、預期或暗示的結果有重大差異。我們也可能受到目前未察覺或目前未認為對我們業務重要的風險影響。
